text:
Clayton Keller is the Mammoth's captain and their power play's whole personality. Nineteen of his 31 points have come with the man advantage, and he's back in the lineup after missing time before returning in Winnipeg on Nov. 23 alongside Dylan Guenther. Friday in Nashville he scored for the first time since Nov. 7.

That drought is mostly bad finishing, not bad hockey. He has six goals on 8.6 expected goals (the quality of his chances) and is shooting 9.5%, below the 12.1% our numbers think is normal for him. The playmaking never stopped: eight assists in his last ten games, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him 98th percentile among forwards for setting up shots last season.

One caution from the other direction. Evolving-Hockey had him sixth among all forwards in wins above replacement last season but flagged that his results ran ahead of his chances, and this year Utah's five-on-five numbers are actually better without him on the ice. Watch his even-strength shifts. If those improve and the shooting normalizes, our range has him at 83 to 109 points.
